rejected_detail: blind#2 (magic color literal 'drifts from tray chips') — premise contradicted by code: draw_tray (app/main.odin:1283,1297) uses the identical literal {238,230,210,255}; no palette field exists for chip bg. Real kernel kept as codebase#2 (third copy of literal).

findings.title: Pause chip overlaps the forecast panel whenever window width < 1220px
findings.evidence: chip := rl.Rectangle{f32(app.view.win_w/2 + 240), 12, 120, 38}  // vs forecast panel card left edge = win_w - 250 (app/render/forecast.odin:62: x := v.win_w - card_w - pad, card_w=230, pad=10)
findings.detail: Chip right edge win_w/2+360 collides with the forecast panel (win_w-250) below win_w=1220. Window is freely resizable (IsWindowResized handler at main.odin:205; no SetWindowSizeMin). At sub-1220 the panel (drawn after, in draw_hud) paints over the chip.
findings.recommended_fix: Clamp chip.x to min(win_w/2+240, win_w-250-124) so the chip never slides under the forecast panel.

findings.title: Paused presentation change (veil removal + edge chip) has zero automated coverage; achievable headless geometry pin skipped
findings.detail: The chip geometry is bespoke and untested; an off-screen/overlapping chip passes the green suite. Pause behavior itself IS covered (core/pause_test.odin, pause.dem T1/T2) — the gap is the cosmetic geometry only. PR body argues the harness cannot capture app overlay (true — adding it would shift every T2 golden); a pure-proc geometry unit test remains achievable.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract chip rect math into a pure proc; unit-test non-overlap vs the health card and forecast panel across win_w values (catches the <1220 case too).

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
findings.detail: P0 pause-determinism path fully covered (158 core tests + 25 goldens green, re-verified locally this round); the only gap is the presentation-layer chip geometry — below the FAIL bar, above PASS.
findings.recommended_fix: The pure-proc geometry pin from the coverage-gap finding raises the gate to PASS.

findings.title: Three 'under the veil' comments survive the veil's removal — comment/code drift
findings.evidence: // fast-path edit THIS frame — the player plans under the veil, and a (193); // under the veil — the live preview + the committed glow stay usable). (220); // 5.3: live while paused too (demolish-and-plan under the veil). (238)
findings.detail: The diff deletes the veil but three comments still reference planning 'under the veil' — stale after this PR.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword the three comments to 'while paused'.

findings.title: Paused chip hardcodes a third copy of the tray-chip bg color literal
findings.detail: The tray-chip bg literal now lives in three places; a future restyle must find them all. (Style itself is consistent — byte-identical to draw_tray's.)
findings.recommended_fix: Hoist a shared TRAY_CHIP_BG constant in app/render and use it in all three sites.

findings.title: Paused-chip x position hand-derives private layout constants of health.odin and forecast.odin — no single source
findings.evidence: // the top-band gap between the Network Health card (right edge at win_w/2 + 230) and the forecast panel (left edge at win_w - 250)
findings.detail: The 240 offset encodes health.odin's card_w=440+pad and forecast.odin's card_w=230+pad by hand; changing either card silently breaks the gap math (comment-only coupling).
findings.recommended_fix: Export the card extents (or a top_band_gap() helper) from app/render and compute the chip anchor from it.

findings.title: Screen-anchored HUD chip drawn inline in main()'s loop; all other persistent HUD chrome lives in draw_hud/render package
findings.evidence: if app.mode == .Paused { ... rl.DrawRectangleRec(chip, ...) } drawn in main loop, before draw_hud(&app)
findings.detail: Persistent HUD chrome convention lives in draw_hud/render; the chip is the one screen-anchored element inline in the main loop (inherited from the old overlay's position, but the overlay was a full-screen effect, not chrome).
findings.recommended_fix: Move the chip draw into draw_hud (or a render proc) alongside the other HUD elements.

findings.title: Opaque pause chip draws after the paused-live demolish popover and can cover its demolish button
findings.evidence: popover drawn at main loop lines 236-241; chip drawn after at 251-265; popover_rect clamps y >= 8 (app/render/popover.odin:44-53)
findings.detail: A pipe popover clamped to y∈[8,22) with x in the chip band puts its bottom button (y≈36-76) partly under the chip's opaque rect (y≤50). Narrow geometry, top-of-screen selection; the chip closed the one previously-free top-edge slot. Button still hit-tests (chip has no hit region) — purely visual.
findings.recommended_fix: Draw the chip before the popover, or add the popover rects to the chip's placement clamp.

findings.title: 'Edits stay live while paused' affordance hint deleted with no replacement
findings.evidence: - draw_text(&app, "P / Space to resume - draw, place, demolish, QoS all live", WIN_W/2 - 292, WIN_H/2 + 14, 18, ...)
findings.detail: The only explicit 'edits work while paused' signal lived in the deleted center hint; the new chip says only 'P/Space to resume'. The always-on HUD hint line still teaches the controls, but not that they stay live paused. Ruling prioritized minimal chrome — flagging for the record, not asking to restore center text.
findings.recommended_fix: If desired, fold 'edits live' into the HUD hint line while paused (top-left, one line).
